restrictions: 135-byte single-block messages; the padded block ends with byte 0x86 (bits 1080..1087 = 01100001), fixing 520 state bits (8 padding + 512 capacity).
Standard SHA3-256 IV (all-zero 1600-bit initial state) and prefix rounds 0..4 of Keccak-f[1600].

All phases (A: trail search, B: 2-round connector with floor mean DF_base >= 25.0, C: space export, E: pairwise disjointness and driver checks, D: online search) are executed and charged under explicit hard primitive-operation counter caps (B_prep = 5430938947579 < 2^42.35, T_max = 5614147877887 < 2^42.40); no external trail, connector or message pair is read. Operative caps are Section 18 of proof.md and tighten the prior 43.0 package.

Preparation charged from measured retired instructions times a measured-mix lambda under a conservative per-class emulation table (7.0 C, 8.4 Python) over C = 1355, enforced on every random tape by hard counter caps B_A = 485271104148, B_B13 = 36318863324, B_B4 = 2905509065916 (5 times E[T_B4]), B_C = 1922076717344 (8 times floor-DF E[T_C]), and B_E = 81763196847 (2 times scaled Phase-E cost) units; online pair enumeration is hard-capped at N_cap = 2^38.40 pairs with early-abort Stage-1 costing 671 ops/pair (B_D = 183208930308 units).

Success probability >= 0.4298 >= 0.40 within T_max = 5614147877887 < 2^42.40 even at the lower end 2^-38.38 of the H1 95% rate interval (prep completion >= 0.6746 times online success >= 0.6372). At the central rate 2^-37.219 the same caps give success >= 0.6047. A doubled lambda raises the chance of hitting a cap and therefore lowers success; it does not raise charged time above the counter caps. The prior 43.0 joint-worst-case figure is not the claim.

Peak memory is strictly below 2^31 bytes on every random tape (380 MiB largest step plus at most M_spaces = 23011 retained spaces; even at 50000 bytes/space this is 1.151e9 < 2^31 bytes); no nonuniform advice.

Three certified 135-byte 5-round collisions from an executed run of the algorithm, plus organizer-executed Docker verification in experiments/r5_connector_verify.py reconstructing the exact DF = 36 connector subspace (rank 1361 -> 1439 -> 1564). The nominal reference identifier does not by itself assert an improvement.

heuristics.statement: For message pairs {x, x xor beta0} enumerated in the exported connector spaces (whose 2-round difference is exactly alpha2 by Lemma 2), the round-2 transition beta2 -> alpha3 and the rounds 3-4 transition to a zero 256-bit digest difference occur with the product of the row-wise DDT probabilities, p = 2^-24 * 2^-13.219 = 2^-37.219 per pair (sum over all alpha4), and distinct pairs behave as independent trials, so N_cap = 2^38.40 pairs succeed with conditional probability at least 1 - exp(-N_cap * 2^-37.219) = 0.8964 at the central rate and at least 1 - exp(-N_cap * 2^-38.38) = 0.6372 at the lower end of the 95% rate interval. Combined with the Section 18 preprocessing completion bound 0.6746, unconditional success is at least 0.4298 >= 0.40 at that lower rate and at least 0.6047 at the central rate.
heuristics.scope: Trail core of Section 3 (beta2/beta3 of Guo et al. core No. 3, translate 8). Measured on the first 33 of the 2,052 exported spaces of base k = 278, seed 1 (base r0, DF 34-38; 2^39.19 pairs), on research-run spaces of other connector bases for the same trail (2^37.23 pairs, 2^39.52 pairs total), and verified on 512 fresh pairs in the organizer-executed experiment r5-stage1-row-filter-audit.
heuristics.extrapolation: The online phase draws up to N_cap = 2^38.40 pairs from randomly ordered spaces of the export, including spaces of the second base and, in other realisations, spaces of other bases that were not measured; the per-pair rate is assumed to be the same there. The collision-count evidence (6 observed vs 4.93 expected) supports the rate within its 95% Poisson interval [2^-38.38, 2^-35.81].
heuristics.limitations: Independence of the round-2..4 events across pairs of one affine space is not proved; stage-1 independence is measured precisely (2^-23.996 vs 2^-24) while the full 2^-37.219 rests on 6 collisions. Because N_cap = 2^38.40 is enforced directly in the hard-capped algorithm, both the central rate and the 2^-38.38 lower confidence bound are covered within T_max = 5614147877887 < 2^42.40 (Section 18).

heuristics.statement: The measured preprocessing programs (phases A-C and E) can be executed on the collision-frontier-v5 256-bit RAM with at most lambda primitive operations per retired AArch64 instruction, where lambda is the measured dynamic opcode mix priced with the per-class emulation table of Section 10.2 (indirect branch 30, flag-setting ALU 7, 64-bit load 7, store 8, sub-word access 12, pair 14, ALU 5, branch 4, multiply 130), plus 0.25 for scalar/vector shared mnemonics: lambda_C = 7.0 for the C trail search and lambda_Py = 8.4 for the Python phases.
heuristics.scope: Opcode histograms of the same programs on AArch64 Linux (DynamoRIO, every executed opcode): three complete connector attempts (success, difference-phase failure, repair failure) and truncated runs of the two C trail-search programs; Apple PMU FP/SIMD share on the macOS connector runs; macOS vs Linux instruction counts on identical inputs for both C programs.
heuristics.extrapolation: The Python mix was measured on connector attempts only; phases A2, A4, B1-B3, C and E use that mix without separate measurement. The Linux (gcc, Debian CPython) mixes are applied to the macOS (clang, Homebrew CPython) runs whose instruction totals are charged; for the C phases the count is scaled by the larger of 1 and the measured gcc/clang instruction ratio.
heuristics.limitations: The per-class costs are an emulation convention, not a verified compilation to the RAM. Because Phases A-C and E are enforced by the Section 18 hard primitive-operation counter caps B_A = 485271104148, B_B13 = 36318863324, B_B4 = 2905509065916, B_C = 1922076717344, and B_E = 81763196847 (total B_prep = 5430938947579 < 2^42.35), any increase in lambda cannot cause charged time to exceed 2^42.40. A doubled lambda (lambda_C = 14.0, lambda_Py = 16.8) makes the B4 cap only 2.5x the doubled expectation and the C cap 4x the doubled floor expectation, so success probability falls; the time counters still hold.

heuristics.statement: With fresh random seeds under the explicit deterministic specification of Section 10.6.2, connector attempts at positions #0-#32 of the k order (k < 278) fail and later attempts succeed independently with probability q' = 3/26 in producing an accepted base pair with DF >= 24 and mean DF_base >= 25.0, so the expected attempt-loop cost is 33 x 2.26e12 + (1/q') x 2.21e12 = 2^46.41 retired instructions (2^39.08 units), and the hard counter cap B_B4 = 2905509065916 units (5 times the central expectation 2^39.08, M_att = 96 attempts) fails with probability at most 1/5 + (1 - 3/26)^63 = 0.20044.
heuristics.scope: Two executed realisations of the attempt loop over the same k order: seeds 1,2,3 (44 attempts, first success #33) and seeds 4,5,6 (48 attempts, first success #41); 3 successes in 92 attempts, none before position #33; all 3 accepted base pairs satisfy DF >= 24 and mean DF_base >= 25.0 (DF 36/35 -> mean 35.5, DF 26/24 -> mean 25.0, DF 27/25 -> mean 26.0); plus organizer-executed reconstruction of the DF = 36 base r0 in experiment r5-connector-subspace-collision.
heuristics.extrapolation: Two realisations are taken as representative of the distribution of the attempt-loop cost and of the accepted base DF for fresh coins; the cut at position #33 was chosen after seeing the data.
heuristics.limitations: The success rate rests on 3 events. Because Phase B4 is hard-capped at B_B4 = 2905509065916 units (5x the central expectation 2^39.08), any lower success rate reduces success probability rather than raising charged time. The claimed 0.40 success probability uses the central q' = 3/26 model inside that cap; it does not also claim the prior package's joint doubled-lambda sensitivity bound of 2^42.19.

heuristics.statement: For an accepted connector base pair with mean degrees of freedom DF_base >= 25.0 (the acceptance floor DF 26/24 enforced by Phase B4), the Phase-C space export keeps at least 85.5% of linearisation seeds as distinct, pairwise-disjoint affine spaces with mean pairs per space at least 2^(DF_base - 1.09) >= 2^23.91, costing at most 1.44e9 retired instructions per seed, so exporting N_cap = 2^38.40 pairs requires M_spaces = 23011 spaces from M_seeds = 26914 seeds. Expected export work at the floor is 26914 x 1.44e9 x 8.4 / 1355 = 2^37.8058 units, and the hard cap B_C = 1922076717344 units is 8x that expectation (Markov failure at most 0.125). Scaled Phase-E work is 2^35.2507 units and fits inside B_E = 81763196847 (2x).
heuristics.scope: Executed Phase-C export on accepted base pair r0/r1 (DF 36/35): 2,400 seeds produced 2,052 distinct pairwise-disjoint spaces (keep rate 0.855, 0 duplicates, all 2,104,326 space pairs verified disjoint) holding 2^45.41 total pairs (mean 2^34.41 = 2^(35.5 - 1.09) pairs/space) at 1.44e9 retired instructions per seed.
heuristics.extrapolation: Extrapolates the keep rate (0.855), per-seed instruction count (1.44e9), and mean space dimension offset (-1.09 bits below base DF) from the executed DF 36/35 export (2,400 seeds) to the acceptance floor DF 26/24. This submission exports N_cap = 2^38.40 pairs, which is M_spaces = 23011 and M_seeds = 26914 at that floor.
heuristics.limitations: Measured on one complete 2,400-seed export for base pair r0/r1 (DF 36/35). Lower-DF accepted bases (down to the enforced floor mean DF_base = 25.0) could exhibit a different keep rate or dimension offset, but Phase C and Phase E are hard-capped at B_C = 1922076717344 units, B_E = 81763196847 units, M_seeds = 26914, and M_spaces = 23011, so neither time nor memory can exceed the Section 18 bounds on any random tape.
